newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bonds ended firmer but off their strongest levels on Tuesday as profit-taking and position squaring ahead of Wednesday's 1997/98 budget eroded much of the market's offshore and local demand-driven gains.
At the local 1400 GMT close, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.795 percent yield after it touched an intraday low of 14.69 percent during the morning session and compared with 14.83 percent overnight.
The market's initial impetus came from offshore demand as well as local short-covering inspired by the issue of three new eurorand issues on Monday.
Dealers said that short-covering by local jobbers looking to go square into Wednesday's 1997/98 budget also helped the market to its intraday low.
"There was quite a lot of demand from offshore and people covering their shorts ahead of the budget," a trader said, adding that market expectations around the budget were generally positive.

Dealers said local institutions had also been keen to take stock on board after having lightened their portfolios during the market's recent correction, while the R150's move below a three-week moving average of 14.77 further spurred demand.

But the morning flurry was followed by a steady erosion of gains in the afternoon session as some players took profits and others squared long positions, leaving the R150 only four basis points firmer from its overnight level.
Dealers said that the market was likely to move sideways on Wednesday morning ahead of Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget announcement at 1215 GMT.
On the currency market, the rand also retraced some of its gains as late importer demand crept into the market to meet earlier offshore and local exporter dollar selling.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4300/4330 against the dollar from 4.4460/4490 overnight.

Dealers said there had been follow-through dollar selling early in the day in the wake of New York selling overnight. This, coupled with local exporter selling, helped the rand to a day's strongest level of 4.4075 bid against the U.S. currency.
But importer demand crept and offset some of the currencies gains, leaving it just over a cent firmer on the day.
"There was a local commercial bank that bought quite a few dollars...I imagine it must have been to cover an importer deal," a trader said.
Dealers said that they expected the rand to remain steady in early Wednesday trade, taking direction from the budget announcement later in the day.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.1064/1157 against sterling after earlier firming to its strongest level in five months, while against the market it was quoted at 0.3848/3852.
On the money market, short-term rates remained steady despite the continuing squeeze on liquidity.
Three-month deposit rates were pegged at between 15.50 and 15.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate held its recent 16.10 to 15.90 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage at 11.171 billion rand on Monday from a record high of 11.680 billion rand on Saturday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners were net buyers of 68.21 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after they sold a net 10.37 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.86 billion rand compared with 2.7 billion rand previously.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
